headline: Barcelona researchers trained an AI to spot ageing in the 3D folding of DNA inside mouse blood stem cells.
score_reason: A modest mouse-cell result (77 percent accuracy) from a paper published on 27 Sep 2026, now surfacing through a press-release site; one point below the pool score for age.
importance_line: Ageing researchers gain a cheap, open image-based test for screening would-be rejuvenation drugs, but the result is in mouse cells, the accuracy is modest and the authors stress it does not show any drug actually made cells younger.
summary: SciTechDaily reports that researchers at IDIBELL, the Barcelona Supercomputing Center and ISGlobal built ChromAgeNet, an image-reading neural network that tells young mouse blood stem cells from aged ones by the three-dimensional arrangement of their DNA, with a 77 percent probability of a correct call in a paper published in Aging Cell on 27 Sep 2026. Because the staining method is cheap and the model small, the team says it could screen many compounds for signs of a younger DNA pattern, though it does not establish that any treatment restored the cells' function.
notes: Score 4 falls below the report cutoff of 5; the main session may hold it back. SciTechDaily appears to rewrite an institutional release and names no other outlet, so it stays the source.
